items.a: God gives you strength for each day. Where you spend it matters.
b: Get the rest you need so you can show up for others.
Give an hour of your energy to someone who’s worn out.
Share a meal with someone who would eat alone.
items.web: He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
items.kjv: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.

items.a: God made you able to picture what isn’t here yet. You can dream up good for someone.
b: Picture what would make someone’s week easier, then do one part.
Make something for someone: a meal, a note, or a drawing.
Imagine how someone else sees things before you answer.
items.web: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works…
items.kjv: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works…

items.a: God lets you choose. Small choices add up to the person you become.
b: Choose one kind thing to do before your next meal.
Choose to let go of one small hurt.
Say no to something so you can say yes to someone.
items.web: Don’t withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it.
items.kjv: Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do it.

items.a: God gave you hands and feet. They can do what words can’t.
b: Help someone carry, fix, or clean something.
Show up in person for someone who’s struggling.
Sit with someone who feels alone.
items.web: Let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.
items.kjv: Let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.

items.a: God gave you a memory. You can hold on to what He’s done and to the people who need you.
b: Remember someone’s name, and use it next time.
Check on someone who had a hard week.
Remember one good thing God did today, and thank Him.
items.web: I remember the days of old. I meditate on all your doings. I contemplate the work of your hands.
items.kjv: I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.

items.a: God gave you a voice. What you say can lift someone up or knock them down.
b: Thank someone for something specific.
Say sorry where you owe it.
Speak up for someone who isn’t in the room.
items.web: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
items.kjv: Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

items.a: God gave you eyes to notice and ears to listen. Paying attention is a way to love.
b: Notice someone others overlook, and say hello.
Listen to someone without fixing or interrupting.
Turn away from what pulls you away from God.
items.web: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Yahweh has made even both of them.
items.kjv: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the LORD hath made even both of them.

items.a: God gave you a mind to learn and understand. What you learn can help others.
b: Learn something that would help someone you know.
Ask what someone meant before you decide.
Help someone think through a problem they’re stuck on.
items.web: The heart of the discerning gets knowledge. The ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
items.kjv: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.

items.a: God made you who you are. The way you are can help someone feel at home.
b: Welcome someone who’s new or left out.
Use your humor, calm, or energy to lift a room.
Be a real friend to someone who needs one.
items.web: As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.
items.kjv: As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

items.a: God gave you feelings. They help you care about what He cares about.
b: Sit with someone who’s sad, and let them be sad.
Celebrate something good in someone else’s life.
Tell God honestly how you feel tonight.
items.web: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
items.kjv: Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.

items.a: God gave you a sense of right and wrong. It’s a quiet nudge worth listening to.
b: Do the right thing you’ve been putting off.
Make it right with someone you’ve hurt.
Ask God to show you what you can’t see in yourself.
items.web: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.
items.kjv: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts…

items.a: God made you to know Him. Your soul is the part of you that talks with Him.
b: Talk to God for a minute before your day starts.
Thank Him for one thing as you fall asleep.
Notice where He’s at work in someone else.
items.web: You shall seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.
items.kjv: And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.

items.a: Aunts, uncles, cousins, grandparents, and in-laws. Family you don’t see every day can still need you.
b: Call a relative you haven’t talked to in a while.
Help a relative with a need they can’t cover right now.
Give an older relative an afternoon: a visit, a ride, or a repair.
items.web: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
items.kjv: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

items.a: Women whose husbands have died. Many are lonely, and some struggle to get by on their own.
b: Invite a widow to share a meal.
Help with a job that’s hard to do alone: a repair, the yard, or paperwork.
Give toward a widow’s groceries, rent, or rides.
items.web: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction…
items.kjv: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction…

items.a: People whose bodies or minds work differently. Many get left out of things others take for granted.
b: Ask what would help, and do that instead of guessing.
Give to a group that helps people with disabilities live, work, and get around.
Offer a ride or your company, and stay a while.
items.web: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind…
items.kjv: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind…

items.a: People without enough: food, a safe place to live, or money for the basics. Some will sleep outside tonight.
b: Give to a food bank or shelter near you.
Give an hour serving at a place that hands out meals.
Carry a few snacks or gift cards to give when someone asks.
items.web: He who has pity on the poor lends to Yahweh…
items.kjv: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD…

items.a: People who left home to start over in a new country. Some ran from war or danger, and many are far from everyone they know.
b: Give to a group that helps new families settle in.
Help someone practice English, fill out a form, or find their way around.
Bring a meal to a new family, and learn their names.
items.web: The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself…
items.kjv: But the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.

items.a: People who are hurt, jailed, or pushed out for what they believe about God.
b: Give to a group that helps people jailed for their faith, and their families.
Write a letter to someone in prison for their faith.
Learn about one place where believing is dangerous, and give there.
items.web: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it.
items.kjv: Whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it…

items.a: Groups that feed, house, heal, and care for people in need. Together, they can help more people than one person can alone.
b: Pick one charity near you, and give to it every month.
Give a few hours of your time, and see the work up close.
Ask a charity what it needs most, and give that.
items.web: Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
items.kjv: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

items.a: People others push out and forget. They can be in prison, sick, old, or treated as not good enough by the people around them.
b: Give to a group that stands up for people no one else will.
Visit someone in prison, a nursing home, or a hospital.
When someone is put down for who they are, stand with them.
items.web: Defend the weak, the poor, and the fatherless. Maintain the rights of the poor and oppressed.
items.kjv: Defend the poor and fatherless: do justice to the afflicted and needy.

items.a: People who left home to feed, heal, teach, and build in another country. Your gift can help them keep serving.
b: Give every month to someone serving far from home.
Send a note from home to cheer them on.
Give to a group that sends doctors, teachers, or builders where they’re needed.
items.web: If you pour out your soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light will rise in darkness…
items.kjv: If thou draw out thy soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul; then shall thy light rise in obscurity…

items.a: People near you who meet to worship God and care for each other and their town.
b: Ask what a church near you needs this month, and help with that.
Give to a church that serves people in your town.
Help with one thing it does for others: a meal, a class, or a ride.
items.web: All who believed were together, and had all things in common.
items.kjv: And all that believed were together, and had all things common…

items.a: Children who’ve lost their parents, or can’t live with them. Every child needs someone who stays.
b: Give to a group that helps foster and adoptive families.
Bring a meal or a gift card to a foster family.
Give your time to mentor a child who needs a steady adult.
items.web: God sets the lonely in families.
items.kjv: God setteth the solitary in families…

items.a: God made the earth and every creature on it, and called it good. Caring for it helps the people who live on it, too.
b: Give to a group that cleans up land, water, or air near you.
Plant something, or help care for a park.
Waste less: fix, share, or give away what you don’t need.
items.web: The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it.
items.kjv: The earth is the LORD’s, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

items.a: The people you grew up with or live with now. They can hurt you most, and need you most.
b: If you were short with someone at home, tell them you’re sorry.
Let go of an old hurt you keep bringing up.
If someone at home has harmed you, peace doesn’t mean staying in harm’s way. Tell someone you trust.
items.web: See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity!
items.kjv: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!

items.a: People you owe money to, or who owe money to you. Money between people can quietly turn into a grudge.
b: If you owe someone, tell them your plan to pay it back.
If someone owes you, ask God whether to let some of it go.
Talk about it face to face, kindly, before it grows.
items.web: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
items.kjv: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.

items.a: The people who lead and care for a church. They carry a lot, and they can get things wrong too.
b: If you’ve held a grudge against a pastor, tell God about it honestly.
Thank a pastor for one specific thing.
If a pastor harmed you, peace doesn’t mean going back. Tell someone you trust.
items.web: And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
items.kjv: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.

items.a: The people you worship with. Being close means you’ll sometimes rub each other the wrong way.
b: If you’ve been avoiding someone at church, say hello this week.
Talk to the person, not about them.
If you caused a hurt, own your part.
items.web: By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.
items.kjv: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.

items.a: The people who live near you, from next door to down the street. You share walls, roads, and noise.
b: Wave, say hello, and learn one neighbor’s name.
If something about them bugs you, talk to them kindly before you complain to others.
Help with something small: a package, a shovel, or a ride.
items.web: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
items.kjv: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

items.a: People on the other side of a vote, a game, a deal, or an argument. You can disagree with them and still treat them with love.
b: Ask how they came to see things the way they do, and listen.
If you said something unkind, tell them you’re sorry.
Let go of something hurtful they said, and pray for them.
items.web: If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.
items.kjv: If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.

items.a: The people you choose to share life with. Small hurts between friends can grow if no one says anything.
b: If you let a friend down, tell them you’re sorry.
If a friend hurt you, tell them gently, then let it go.
Reach out to a friend you’ve drifted from.
items.web: He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.
items.kjv: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.

items.a: Groups you’re part of for fun or a cause: teams, clubs, classes, and online groups.
b: Make peace with someone you’ve been competing with.
Welcome someone who seems left out.
If you’ve been part of the gossip, stop, and make it right.
items.web: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
items.kjv: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

items.a: People you don’t know: a driver, a cashier, or someone online. A short moment can still leave a mark.
b: If you were rude to a stranger, do a kindness for the next one.
Be patient with someone who’s slow or having a hard day.
Think before you post about someone you don’t know.
items.web: As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.
items.kjv: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.

items.a: The people you work or study with. You spend hours together, and pressure brings out the worst in everyone.
b: If you blamed someone for your mistake, set it straight.
Let go of a slight, and greet them like normal tomorrow.
Give credit to someone who earned it.
items.web: Let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger…
items.kjv: Let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath…

items.a: People whose race, language, or customs are different from yours. Hurts between groups run deep, and healing starts with how you treat one person.
b: Get to know someone from another culture: ask about their family or their food.
If you’ve laughed at a joke about their people, stop, and don’t pass it on.
If you hurt someone, ask them to forgive you, and listen to how it felt.
items.web: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free man, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
items.kjv: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.

items.a: People who wish you harm, or who you wish harm on. Jesus asks something hard here, and He helps you do it.
b: Pray for them, even if it’s one sentence.
Turn down one chance to get back at them.
If someone has harmed you, peace doesn’t mean going back. You can forgive from a safe distance.
items.web: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink…
items.kjv: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink…

items.a: Anything you put ahead of God: money, success, a person, or your phone. It’s whatever you trust or want most.
b: Notice what you reach for first when you’re worried, and bring that worry to God instead.
Give God the first few minutes of your day, before your screen.
Hold one good thing more loosely: thank God for it instead of chasing more.
items.web: Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
items.kjv: Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

items.a: Thinking you’re better than others, or that you don’t need God or anyone else. It makes it hard to say “I was wrong.”
b: Say “I was wrong” to someone this week.
Let someone else get the credit.
Ask for help with something you’ve been doing alone.
items.web: God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
items.kjv: God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.

items.a: Saying what isn’t true, or leaving out what is, so things go your way. It makes it hard for people to trust you.
b: Tell the whole story, even the part that makes you look bad.
Say “I don’t know” when you don’t know.
If you stretched the truth this week, set it straight.
items.web: Therefore, putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbor, for we are members of one another.
items.kjv: Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.

items.a: Wishing someone harm, or treating them like they don’t matter. It often starts small, with contempt or an insult.
b: Name the person you resent, and ask God to help you see them as He does.
Stop yourself before you insult someone, even in your head.
Do one kind thing for someone you can’t stand.
items.web: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
items.kjv: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.

items.a: Letting drink, screens, shopping, or anything else take more of you than it should. Self-control means you’re in charge, not the habit.
b: Pick one thing you overdo, and set a small limit for this week.
When you feel the pull, pause and pray one sentence first.
If you can’t stop on your own, tell someone you trust and get help.
items.web: For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
items.kjv: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

items.a: Looking at someone as something to use, instead of a whole person God made. Sexual integrity means keeping your promises and treating people with respect.
b: Turn away from what feeds it: a show, a site, or a habit.
When you notice someone, remember they’re a whole person with a story.
Keep the promises you’ve made to the people you love.
items.web: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
items.kjv: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

items.a: Treating people in charge, like a boss, a teacher, or a leader, as if they don’t deserve basic respect. You can disagree and still be respectful.
b: Disagree with a boss or leader to their face, kindly, instead of behind their back.
Stop mocking a leader, even one you didn’t choose.
Pray for someone in charge whose choices worry you.
items.web: Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.
items.kjv: Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.

items.a: Breaking the trust someone gave you: telling a secret, breaking a promise, or turning on someone who counted on you.
b: Keep a secret someone trusted you with.
If you broke a promise, own it, and make it right.
Stand by a friend when it would be easier not to.
items.web: One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
items.kjv: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.

items.a: Wanting what someone else has, and feeling worse because they have it. It steals the joy from what God already gave you.
b: Thank God for three things you already have.
Be glad out loud for someone who got what you wanted.
Take a break from what feeds it, like scrolling through other people’s lives.
items.web: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
items.kjv: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.

items.a: Putting what you want ahead of what others need, again and again. Love looks out for other people.
b: Let someone else choose this time.
Notice one need around you today, and meet it.
Give up something you want so someone else can have it.
items.web: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
items.kjv: Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

items.a: Always wanting more, even when you have enough, or wanting what belongs to someone else.
b: Give away something you don’t need this week.
Before you buy, ask: do I need this, or do I just want more?
Return anything you’ve kept that isn’t yours.
items.web: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance, with increase…
items.kjv: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase…

items.a: Using up or throwing away what God made as if it didn’t matter: food, water, things, and the earth itself.
b: Use what you have before you buy more.
Pick up trash you didn’t drop.
Turn off, unplug, or save one thing you usually waste.
items.web: Yahweh, how many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches.
items.kjv: O LORD, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all: the earth is full of thy riches.

items.a: Keeping for yourself what God gave you to share: money, time, skills, or things you never use.
b: Give away something you’ve been holding onto for no reason.
Share a skill with someone who could use it.
Set aside part of what you earn to give, before you spend the rest.
items.web: It is more blessed to give than to receive.
items.kjv: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

items.a: Using someone’s art, music, photos, or writing without asking. A real person made it, and it’s theirs to share.
b: Ask before you use someone’s photo, art, or words, and say who made it.
If you used someone’s work without asking, ask now, or take it down.
When you can, pay the person who made it: a local artist, a friend’s band, or a writer you love.
items.web: The laborer is worthy of his wages.
items.kjv: The labourer is worthy of his reward.

items.a: Passing on something about someone that hurts their good name, true or not. A rumor or a cruel joke can take a good name away.
b: If you passed on a rumor, go back and set it straight.
Say something good about them to the people who heard it.
If they know what you said, ask them to forgive you.
items.web: A good name is more desirable than great riches…
items.kjv: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches…

items.a: Taking money that isn’t yours by a trick: on taxes, a bill, a bet, or a deal. It can feel small, but someone always pays.
b: If you underpaid someone, go back and pay what you owe.
Fix a mistake in your favor, like extra change or a missed charge.
Pay people fairly and on time.
items.web: Better is a little with righteousness, than great revenues with injustice.
items.kjv: Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right.

items.a: Turning people against someone, or pulling a friend away from another, so you come out on top.
b: Stop passing on complaints that drive people apart.
Speak well of the person you’ve been turning others against.
Help two people who’ve drifted apart find their way back.
items.web: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
items.kjv: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

items.a: Selling something by saying it’s better than it is, or by hiding what’s wrong with it.
b: If you sold something with a problem, tell the buyer and make it right.
Describe what you sell honestly, flaws and all.
Before you share an ad or a deal, check that it’s true.
items.web: Getting treasures by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor…
items.kjv: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a vanity tossed to and fro…

items.a: Taking something that belongs to someone else, or borrowing it and never giving it back.
b: Return what you borrowed, even if it’s been a long time.
Pay back what you took, and add something extra.
Ask forgiveness from the person you took from.
items.web: Let him who stole steal no more; but rather let him labor, producing with his hands something that is good, that he may have something to give to him who has need.
items.kjv: Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.

items.a: Leading someone to believe what isn’t true, by what you say or what you leave out, so you get something from them.
b: Tell the person what really happened.
Fix the wrong idea you gave them, even if it costs you.
Make good on anything you got by misleading them.
items.web: Truth’s lips will be established forever, but a lying tongue is only momentary.
items.kjv: The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment.

items.a: Giving people a wrong picture of God by how you treat them: harsh, unfair, or unkind in His name.
b: Apologize to someone you treated badly while talking about God.
Show someone what God is like with a kindness, not a lecture.
Let people see you own your mistakes.
items.web: Let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
items.kjv: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

items.a: Passing off someone else’s idea or work as your own, or letting people think you did what they did.
b: Tell people whose idea it really was.
Thank them in front of the people who heard.
Share the credit next time, even when no one would notice.
items.web: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.
items.kjv: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.

items.a: Walking away from someone who counted on you, or going after what was theirs: their place, their partner, or their friends.
b: Go back to someone you left without a word, and make it right.
Keep showing up for someone, even when it costs you.
Ask forgiveness from someone who felt you left them behind.
items.web: There is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
items.kjv: There is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.

items.a: Harm you didn’t mean to cause: something broken, lost, or forgotten. It still matters to the person it happened to.
b: Own it out loud: “That was my fault.”
Fix it, replace it, or pay for it.
Ask what would help, then do it.
items.web: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed.
items.kjv: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.

lists.name: Faith Family
lists.a: The people you grow with: anyone you can talk with about God and what matters most.
b: A friend you can talk with about God.
Someone you pray with, or who prays for you.
Someone who helped you know God better.
lists.web: I thank my God whenever I remember you…
lists.kjv: I thank my God upon every remembrance of you…

lists.name: Family & Friends
lists.a: The people closest to you: the family you live with or grew up with, and the friends you count on.
b: The people you live with, or the family you call most.
A friend you’d call on a hard day.
Someone close you haven’t talked to in a while.
lists.web: If they fall, the one will lift up his fellow…
lists.kjv: If they fall, the one will lift up his fellow…

lists.name: Neighbors
lists.a: The people around you, from next door to the checkout line. You see them often, but you may not know them well.
b: Someone who lives on your street or in your building.
A coworker, a classmate, or someone at the gym.
Someone who serves you: a cashier, a driver, or a mail carrier.
lists.web: A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.
lists.kjv: Better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.

lists.name: Leaders
lists.a: People with a say over your life: at work, at school, at church, and in your town or country. Their choices touch many people.
b: A boss, a teacher, or a coach.
A pastor, or someone who leads a group you’re in.
A leader in your town or country, even one whose choices worry you.
lists.web: …prayers… be made for all men, for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life…
lists.kjv: …prayers… be made for all men; for kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life…

lists.name: The Hurting
lists.a: People who are grieving, sick, forgotten, or alone. Some will tell you. Others keep it quiet.
b: Someone who is sick, or caring for someone who is.
Someone who lost a person they love.
Someone who seems lonely, or who hasn’t been around lately.
lists.web: Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.
lists.kjv: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart…

lists.name: Difficult People
lists.a: People it’s hard to love right now: someone who hurt you, works against you, or gets under your skin. Praying for them doesn’t mean letting them hurt you.
b: Someone you’re upset with right now.
Someone who works against you, or who you compete with.
Someone who hurt you. You can pray for them from a safe distance.
lists.web: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
lists.kjv: Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you, bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.

lists.name: Your Requests
lists.a: What you’re asking God for yourself, big or small. You can bring Him anything.
b: Something you’re worried about.
A choice you need help making.
A change you’d like to see in yourself.
lists.web: Cast your burden on Yahweh and he will sustain you.
lists.kjv: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee…
